claims.text: Medicines work best when taken before motion starts
claims.quote: Individuals should be advised that medication is most effective when taken before exposure, rather than after the onset of symptoms.

claims.text: Once nausea is established, gastric slowing can make oral absorption less reliable
claims.quote: Once the initial symptoms of motion sickness begin, gastric stasis may prevent absorption.

claims.text: CDC lists an estimated 6-to-8-hour onset for the Transderm Scop patch (Table 7.6.2)
claims.quote: Scopolamine | Transderm Scop | Transdermal | 1 mg | 6–8 | 72

claims.text: Drowsiness is the most common effect; less drowsy is not no drowsiness
claims.quote: The most common side effect is drowsiness or sedation. Scopolamine is slightly less sedating than dimenhydrinate or meclizine, whereas promethazine is the most sedating.

claims.text: Avoid alcohol
claims.quote: Alcohol consumption and smoking (nicotine) should be avoided because they increase motion sickness.

claims.text: CDC suggests considering a trial dose before departure
claims.quote: Because side effects differ among travelers, consider recommending a trial dose of one or more medications before departure.

claims.text: Do not cut the patch
claims.quote: The transdermal patch should never be cut up in mistaken attempts to vary the dose, since this disrupts the mechanism of release.

claims.text: Sensory conflict between eyes, inner ear and body sense
claims.quote: The most widely accepted explanation for motion sickness is the sensory conflict or neural mismatch theory.

claims.text: Horizon view, avoiding close visual tasks and head movements reduce conflicting signals
claims.quote: behavioral countermeasures, such as obtaining a horizon view and avoiding visual tasks, are based on reducing visual-vestibular mismatches

claims.text: Typical features include nausea, vomiting, pallor, sweating, dizziness, yawning, fatigue or drowsiness
claims.quote: Patterns of symptoms vary but usually progress from initial symptoms, such as stomach awareness, feelings of warmth, yawning, sweating, dizziness, through to nausea and ultimately to vomiting.

claims.text: Controlled breathing can be a useful measure
claims.quote: Laboratory trials show this strategy to be around half as effective as anti-motion-sickness drugs; unlike drugs, it is free of side effects

claims.text: Habituation can help but is stimulus-specific and may take time
claims.quote: Can be slow to acquire, often stimulus-specific; it may need periodic re-exposure to motion to maintain adaptive protection

claims.text: Adequate rest helps
claims.quote: Being sleep-deprived can worsen motion sickness.

claims.text: CDC describes the evidence for diets, supplements and ginger as weak and contradictory
claims.quote: The efficacy of particular diets, supplements, vitamins, ginger, and so on, has only weak and contradictory supporting evidence.

claims.text: Laboratory trials of acupressure bands have not shown them to outperform placebo
claims.quote: Laboratory trials show that acupressure bands or similar treatments are no more effective than placebo.

claims.text: Minimally sedating antihistamines such as loratadine and fexofenadine are not effective because they do not reach the brain
claims.quote: The newer, "minimally sedating" antihistamines (e.g., cetirizine, fexofenadine, loratadine) are not effective for treatment of motion sickness because they are designed to avoid penetration into the brain.

claims.text: CDC states 5-HT3 antiemetics such as ondansetron are not effective against motion sickness
claims.quote: Other antiemetics such as the highly potent 5-HT3 antagonists (ondansetron and granisetron) are not effective against motion sickness because their sites of action are not at the central vestibular centers of the brain.

claims.text: Not every dizzy spell is motion sickness; other causes need excluding
claims.quote: For healthcare professionals managing a traveler with acute symptoms consistent with motion sickness, other causes should be excluded, including peripheral and central vestibular disease.

claims.text: Repeated vomiting should prompt a hydration assessment
claims.quote: Ensure adequate fluid and electrolyte intake if the individual is vomiting.

claims.text: Persistent rocking after travel (post-disembarkation) needs evaluation, not self-treatment
claims.quote: A very rare condition termed mal de debarquement syndrome involves symptoms persisting for weeks or more. For such cases, the traveler should be referred to a medical specialist in vestibular disorders.

claims.text: Glaucoma or urinary history can change the choice
claims.quote: Scopolamine should not be used in travelers with glaucoma or who are at risk of prostatic urinary retention.

claims.text: Match the ingredient and timing to the trip (exposure length)
claims.quote: The following general recommendations can aid in choosing the preferred drugs for adults:

claims.text: Prescription patch indicated in adults for prevention of motion-sickness nausea and vomiting
claims.quote: TRANSDERM SCŌP is an anticholinergic indicated in adults for the prevention of: •nausea and vomiting associated with motion sickness.

claims.text: One patch behind one ear at least 4 hours before effect is needed, up to 3 days
claims.quote: Apply one TRANSDERM SCŌP transdermal system to the hairless area behind one ear at least 4 hours before the antiemetic effect is required – for use up to 3 days.

claims.text: If continuing, remove the old system and apply a new one behind the other ear
claims.quote: If therapy is required for longer than 3 days, remove the first transdermal system and apply a new TRANSDERM SCŌP transdermal system behind the other ear.

claims.text: Wear only one at a time; do not cut
claims.quote: •Only wear one transdermal system at any time.•Do not cut the transdermal system.

claims.text: Each system contains 1.3 mg of scopolamine
claims.quote: Each system contains 1.3 mg of scopolamine base.

claims.text: Formulated to deliver approximately 1 mg over 3 days
claims.quote: Each TRANSDERM SCŌP transdermal system is formulated to deliver in vivo approximately 1 mg of scopolamine over 3 days.

claims.text: Scopolamine can reduce sweating and raise core temperature; external heat worsens it
claims.quote: Anticholinergic agents, including scopolamine, can increase core body temperature and reduce sweating, which may cause further increases in body temperature. Hyperthermia may be exacerbated by exposure to external heat sources or high environmental temperature.

claims.text: Symptoms may persist after removal because absorption continues through the skin
claims.quote: Symptoms may persist following removal of the used transdermal system as there may be continued systemic absorption of scopolamine through the skin.

claims.text: If unusually hot or not sweating, remove the patch and contact a healthcare professional
claims.quote: Advise patients if body temperature increases, or they are not sweating in warm environmental conditions, to remove the transdermal system and contact their healthcare provider.

claims.text: Contraindicated in angle-closure glaucoma and hypersensitivity to belladonna alkaloids
claims.quote: hypersensitivity to scopolamine or other belladonna alkaloids or to any ingredient or component in the formulation or delivery system.

claims.text: Open-angle glaucoma requires monitoring
claims.quote: Monitor intraocular pressure in patients with open angle glaucoma and adjust glaucoma therapy during TRANSDERM SCŌP use, as needed.

claims.text: Eye pain, red eyes, blurred vision or halos: remove the system and get medical advice
claims.quote: Advise patients to immediately remove the transdermal system and contact their healthcare provider if they experience symptoms of acute angle closure glaucoma (e.g., eye pain or discomfort, blurred vision, visual halos or colored images

claims.text: Urinary retention warning; difficulty urinating
claims.quote: Scopolamine, due to its anticholinergic properties, can decrease gastrointestinal motility and cause urinary retention.

claims.text: Confusion and cognitive effects; severe persistent symptoms need medical attention
claims.quote: Scopolamine can cause drowsiness, disorientation, and confusion. Discontinue TRANSDERM SCŌP if signs or symptoms of cognitive impairment develop. If, despite this, the symptoms persist in a severe form, instruct patients to seek medical attention.

claims.text: Can impair driving and machinery; alcohol and sedatives add to it
claims.quote: TRANSDERM SCŌP may impair the mental and/or physical abilities required for the performance of hazardous tasks such as driving a motor vehicle, operating machinery or participating in underwater sports.

claims.text: Avoid alcohol with the patch
claims.quote: You should not drink alcohol while using TRANSDERM SCŌP. It can increase your chances of having serious side effects.

claims.text: Combining with meclizine or other sedating drugs can increase effects
claims.quote: have anticholinergic properties (e.g., other belladonna alkaloids, sedating antihistamines, meclizine, tricyclic antidepressants, and muscle relaxants) may potentiate the effects of TRANSDERM SCŌP

claims.text: Withdrawal symptoms 24 hours or more after removal include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, balance disturbance
claims.quote: Discontinuation of TRANSDERM SCŌP, usually after several days of use, may result in withdrawal symptoms, such as disturbances of equilibrium, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, sweating, headache, mental confusion

claims.text: Withdrawal onset 24 hours or more after removal
claims.quote: The onset of these symptoms is generally 24 hours or more after the transdermal system has been removed.

claims.text: Transferred drug can dilate a pupil or blur vision; wash hands
claims.quote: Scopolamine can cause temporary dilation of the pupils resulting in blurred vision if it comes in contact with the eyes.

claims.text: Remove before MRI
claims.quote: Remove TRANSDERM SCŌP before undergoing an MRI.

claims.text: Dry mouth, drowsiness and visual effects are common
claims.quote: Motion Sickness (>15%): dry mouth, drowsiness, blurred vision and dilation of the pupils.

claims.text: Not for children (no pediatric pathway)
claims.quote: TRANSDERM SCŌP is not approved for use in pediatric patients

claims.text: Older adults more vulnerable
claims.quote: elderly patients had an increased risk of neurologic and psychiatric adverse reactions, such as hallucinations, confusion, dizziness and drug withdrawal syndrome

claims.text: Patient information calls for discussing pregnancy and breastfeeding
claims.quote: are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if TRANSDERM SCŌP can harm your unborn baby.

claims.text: Conflict between eyes, inner ear and body sense
claims.quote: The principal sensors are the eyes, the vestibular apparatus, and proprioceptive receptors.

claims.text: Environmental measures may be enough for some adults
claims.quote: In most cases, motion sickness can be prevented by behavioral and environmental modifications (avoidance, habituation, and minimization of motion stimuli).

claims.text: Medicines work better as prevention; gastric stasis limits oral absorption
claims.quote: Anti-motion sickness medications are helpful when given prophylactically. They are less effective for treatment because motion sickness may induce gastric stasis that interferes with the absorption of the medications given orally.

claims.text: Choice depends on the trip and the person
claims.quote: The types of medication used should depend on the duration of exposure, the susceptibility of the individual to motion sickness and the severity of expected symptoms, the incidence and severity of adverse events

claims.text: Migraine, inner-ear disorders, stroke and other conditions overlap with motion sickness
claims.quote: Differential diagnosis of motion sickness includes migraine, pregnancy, concussion, intoxication, hangover, basilar artery occlusion, cerebral vascular accident, vestibulopathy, hypoglycemia, depression, and anxiety.

claims.text: Repeated vomiting can lead to dehydration

claims.text: Review gives 72 hours in another section

claims.text: Second-generation antihistamines not effective

claims.text: Scopolamine adverse effects include urinary retention and confusion
claims.quote: Less common adverse events include headache, drowsiness, confusion, palpitations, tachycardia, bloating, constipation, and urinary retention.
